sources.entry: Retrom - Private cloud game library distribution server + frontend/launcher. GPL-3.0 Docker/Rust

summary.one_liner: Retrom is a self-hosted game library server with desktop, web, and launcher clients, focused on managing and launching emulated and DRM-free games.
summary.what_it_does: Retrom runs a centralized service on one device that hosts a game library, which clients on other devices can connect to in order to install, uninstall, download, and play games. It can scan the filesystem for games and platforms and add them to the library automatically. Clients are offered for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and a web client provides library access from a browser, including in-browser emulation via EmulatorJS. Emulator profiles are managed per client and stored on the server so they can be shared or restored, and games can be launched through those profiles from one interface. The README also lists unifying third-party libraries (Steam, with GoG marked as upcoming and native PC/Linux/macOS games as experimental), and automatic download of metadata and artwork from supported providers such as IGDB.
use_cases: self-host a personal game library server
stream or download games to multiple desktop machines
manage and launch emulator games from one library
play DRM-free games from a browser
sync emulator configuration profiles across devices
auto-fetch game artwork and metadata for a collection
how_to_run: Follow the quick start guide linked in the README (external wiki)
Download the latest client from the README's download link
notable: Emulator profiles stored on the server and shared across clients
Web client with in-browser emulation via EmulatorJS
Automatic metadata and artwork via IGDB provider
caveats: Authentication for multiple users is still unchecked on the roadmap, so multi-user auth is not yet available
Roadmap lists server binaries as not yet published, so Docker is the server deployment path
GoG support is marked 'soon' and native PC/Linux/macOS game support is experimental
Roadmap is noted as often out of date; the full roadmap lives on the wiki
